findings.claim: PRD says PreCompact is not used, but ADR-0009 says VS Code delivers compaction memory via a compaction hook marker; on VS Code that hook is PreCompact.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:268 'Not used: PreCompact'; adr/0009:96 'Gemini, Copilot CLI, VS Code | the compaction hook writes meta(pending_compact...)'; spike-hooks-verified.md:56 'VS Code | PreCompact marker -> UserPromptSubmit additionalContext'. v1 configs/vscode-copilot/hooks.json registers PreCompact.
findings.fix: PRD 15.3: list PreCompact (VS Code, Copilot CLI preCompact, Gemini PreCompress) as a 5th event used only for the marker, or state the marker comes from elsewhere.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 75ae6ae3 2026-03-05 'feat: multi-platform adapters, session continuity, hook scripts' (VS Code PreCompact hook). REGRESSION_RISK: dropping it loses memory after compaction on VS Code. SAFE_FIX: keep PreCompact for marker only.

findings.claim: 'VS Code: rewrite supported' has no evidence. The hook spike lists only additionalContext and permissionDecision for VS Code PreToolUse.
findings.evidence: spike-hooks-verified.md:18 VS Code PreToolUse 'additionalContext | permissionDecision / exit 2'; no updatedInput. v1 hooks/core/formatters.mjs:92-99 emits updatedInput for vscode-copilot but no test proves the host applies it.
findings.fix: Mark the VS Code case B row [U] and add a source check in vscode-copilot-chat (toolCalling.tsx hook result handling) or treat VS Code like Kiro until proved.
findings.archaeology: formatters.mjs vscode modify shape from fc6f0a1f 2026-03-13 'fix: use correct Claude Code hook field names for PreToolUse responses (#110)': copied Claude Code shape, not VS Code proof.

findings.claim: Subagent detection is only for Claude Code (agent_type payload, .claude/agents/*.md). Nothing says how VS Code subagents (runSubagent, .agent.md custom agents) are detected or what tools they have, yet the VS Code row claims cases A/B/C.
findings.evidence: adr/0016:17-19 only agent_type + .claude/agents; spike-hooks-verified.md:37 VS Code payload: 'hook_event_name; session_id, transcript_path optional' (no agent_type); hooks come also from '.agent.md'.
findings.fix: Add a VS Code row to 'How the subagent's tools are known' or state the safe default (no ctx tools) and a live/source check.

findings.claim: ctx_upgrade install modes do not cover VS Code Copilot (also Kiro, ZCode). VS Code has a host plugin path with its own update command.
findings.evidence: adr/0010:42 lists 'Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Qwen, Copilot CLI'; :43 'Pi, OpenCode 2, manual'. spike-distribution.md:20 'VS Code Copilot | /plugin install <git-repo or mkt> ... | /plugin update <plugin>'.
findings.fix: Add VS Code (Agent Plugins, /plugin update) to the host-managed list, and give Kiro/ZCode an explicit mode.

findings.claim: VS Code v1 footprint lists only .github/hooks/context-mode.json; v1 also writes session data to <project>/.github/context-mode/sessions/ or ~/.vscode/context-mode/sessions/.
findings.fix: Add both data dirs to the VS Code row (project one is inside a committed .github tree; report, delete only after prompt).
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 75ae6ae3 2026-03-05; #649 added CONTEXT_MODE_DATA_DIR override. Cleanup must honor that override too.

findings.claim: Tool-name table says VS Code is mcp_<server>_<tool> but does not flag that v1 uses context-mode_<tool> for VS Code (as it flags v1 Gemini at :196), and does not say which name hook payloads carry.
findings.evidence: cm-main hooks/core/tool-naming.mjs:26 '"vscode-copilot": (tool) => `context-mode_${tool}`' from 2b5cfef7 2026-03-21 (#158 #163 #164). spike-hooks-verified.md:37 'names are VS Code names (runInTerminal)'.
findings.fix: Add a 'v1 is wrong about VS Code' note and a GP3 fixture with a recorded VS Code hook payload for an MCP tool.
findings.archaeology: 2b5cfef7 ORIGINAL_INTENT 'OpenCode/VS Code Copilot: <server>_<tool>'. v2 changing it is a fix if the source check holds; test-gate it.

findings.claim: Generated hook matchers are the stated filter, but VS Code likely ignores matchers, so the script must filter tool_name itself.
findings.evidence: spike-hooks-verified.md:37 'Matchers likely ignored -> filter tool_name in script'.
findings.fix: State that the VS Code adapter filters by tool_name in code and test it with a non-matching payload.

findings.claim: VS Code project source = ${workspaceFolder}, but it does not expand for extension-registered servers; v2 installs VS Code as an Agent Plugin, which may hit that case.
findings.evidence: spike-project-source.md:42 'VS Code Copilot | yes (not for extension-registered servers, vscode#272420)'; PRD-v2.md:94.
findings.fix: Add a contract check that ${workspaceFolder} expands for the plugin-installed server, else define the error (no fallback).
findings.archaeology: v1 used VSCODE_CWD (3d3e4248 2026-05-24, #692); #1032/#1033 show it is wrong under Remote-WSL, so dropping it is correct.

findings.claim: VS Code with chat.useClaudeHooks also runs .claude/settings.json hooks, so a user with both Claude Code and VS Code installs gets double hook runs. No doc covers this.
findings.evidence: spike-hooks-verified.md:37 '.claude/settings.json if chat.useClaudeHooks (double-run risk)'; v1 copilot-base.ts:336-341 reads .claude/settings.json as fallback.
findings.fix: Add a dedupe rule (hook checks the host from payload/env and exits on the wrong adapter) and a doctor check.
